definitions.explanation: Hair that has become messy or stuck out at odd angles from sleeping on it.

examples.japanese: {寝癖|ねぐせ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ひどい→ひどい：01097_hidoi⟧。
{寝癖|ねぐせ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{直|なお}して→直す：00869_naosu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{出|で}かけた→出かける：00833_dekakeru⟧。
examples.english: I fixed my bed hair before going out.

examples.japanese: {寝癖|ねぐせ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ついたまま⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{来|き}て→来る：00254_kuru⟧しまって⟦{恥|は}ずかしかった→恥ずかしい：00843_hazukashii⟧。
examples.english: I was embarrassed that I came to the office with bed hair still sticking up.

notes:
{寝癖|ねぐせ} refers to hair that has become messy or sticks out at odd angles from sleeping. Composed of {寝|ね} (sleep) + ⟦{癖|くせ}→癖：03814_kuse⟧ (habit/tendency). Also written as {寝|ね}ぐせ in mixed script.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {寝癖|ねぐせ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧つく: to get bed hair
- {寝癖|ねぐせ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{直|なお}す: to fix bed hair
- {寝癖|ねぐせ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ひどい→ひどい：01097_hidoi⟧: to have bad bed hair
- {寝癖|ねぐせ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ついたまま: with bed hair still sticking up

FIXING BED HAIR:
Japanese people typically fix {寝癖|ねぐせ} by wetting the hair with ⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧ (water) or using a ⟦{櫛|くし}→櫛：03882_kushi⟧ (comb). Some use {寝癖|ねぐせ}{直|なお}し⟦スプレー→スプレー：11581_supuree⟧ (bed-hair-fixing spray).

USAGE:
A relatable everyday topic in Japanese conversation — talking about one's {寝癖|ねぐせ} is common and lighthearted.
